in_hebrew.name: רחל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The name Rachel in Hebrew (רחל) is derived from the Hebrew root רחל (rchl), which means 'euphonic' or 'radiant'. This name is believed to have been given to the biblical figure Rachel, who is described as a beautiful and beloved wife of the patriarch Jacob. In the Bible, Rachel is also the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.

in_greek.name: Ραχέλ
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Rachelle in Greek (Ραχέλ) is derived from the Hebrew name Rachel. In Greek, the name Rachelle means 'euphony' or 'beauty'. The name Rachel was given to the biblical figure Rachel, who is described as a beautiful and beloved wife of the patriarch Jacob. In the New Testament, there is a mention of Rachel's tomb in Bethlehem.

in_latin.name: Rachelis
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Rachelle in Latin (Rachelis) is derived from the Hebrew name Rachel. In Latin, the name Rachelle means 'euphony' or 'beauty'. The name Rachel was given to the biblical figure Rachel, who is described as a beautiful and beloved wife of the patriarch Jacob. In Latin literature, the name Rachelis is found in the works of authors such as Ovid and Virgil.
